title: mmd、ZRAM writeback/recompression 与厂商内存拓展
key_conclusions: ZRAM compression, recompression, writeback, and vendor memory extension are separate mechanisms with separate evidence.
writeback can reduce RAM pressure but may add storage latency on later fault-in.
mmd and vendor memory extension features must be treated as ROM-specific policy rather than universal AOSP behavior.
PSI, mm_stat, bd_stat, vmstat, and logs must be sampled in the same window before tuning conclusions.
shallow_points: The article does not include real bd_stat samples from devices with ZRAM writeback enabled.
It does not validate mmd source paths or properties for a specific Android vendor branch.
It does not quantify storage latency and flash wear tradeoffs.
It does not include before/after data for recompression policy changes.
discovered_connections: Day 58's ZRAM cost model expands into CPU compression, denser recompression, and backing-storage writeback.
Day 57 victim analysis needs writeback state because kill benefit and fault-in latency can change after cold pages move.
Day 52 PSI remains the user-visible gate for judging whether memory extension is helping or hurting.
Day 60 should connect system memory pressure with app compaction and trim opportunities before lmkd kills.

knowledge_gaps: Need real writeback-enabled devices to validate bd_stat fields and sysfs permissions.
